scope: Bounded control-lane pipelining and unchanged local density profiles.
implementation: At most eight already-budgeted FIFO control frames share one peer connection; no wait to fill the window and no new connections or raised budgets. Bulk data stays one frame at a time.
Ordered writes and reads run concurrently to avoid full-buffer deadlock. The existing I/O deadline bounds the entire window.
Each response keeps its authenticated channel/request/sequence/route binding. Revalidate routes before sending, after receiving and before notifying observers.

On connection failure, retain observed earlier admissions, fail unresolved frames, close the stream and never replay the partially sent window automatically. Admissions never replace durable Raft responses.
Payloads and node/peer permits release before observer completion; dropped observers cannot release physical work before joined shutdown.

reproducer.result: Original sender times out waiting for the second frame while the first admission reply is withheld. The final test receives exactly eight frames before replies and keeps the ninth queued.
reproducer.test_repairs: The initial test compile used a raw integer for LogIndex. The first pipeline prototype reached the later no-commit assertion, which incorrectly assumed bootstrap commit zero. Final tests compare before/after committed positions, preserving the no-advancement property; all original outputs are retained.

negative_cases: lost reply preserves only verified prefix

comparison_scope: The retained earlier density failures remain failed at their original pins. Workload/profile and offered-route identities can be compared, but short runs on a shared host do not establish a causal speedup or sustained capacity.
limitations: One shared Mac, one Colima VM, at most five 1-vCPU/3-GiB/no-swap Cellar nodes and RustFS; no independent failure domains or Amazon S3 qualification.

Control queues still fill during the 1,500-cell measured run. Mean CPU does not rule out the shorter pressure burst visible in Docker samples; SQL-stage bounds identify a phase, not a proven causal sub-operation.

Only 30 active cells at 10 operations/second with Quorum acknowledgements and 100 ms ticks. Q1 retains six processes, 10,000 cells, different active fraction/data distribution/tick interval, and a 24-hour soak.
No group-limit increase. Q1 average 5,000 replicas/process still exceeds the 4,096 bound before reserve. Instrumentation overhead and whole-device attribution remain open.
Exact owned containers are stopped and their empty networks removed; volumes remain. The dedicated profile is stopped; other profiles were not mutated.
remaining: Repeatable sustained and S3-durable latency, controlled equivalent-contract Fleet/bucket fault baselines and Q1 qualification.
